I need to do a holistic audit of the jaimeibrahim.com portfolio site after completing major revisions. The site is a Next.js 15 App Router portfolio for a Brand Design Director.

Read these key files to understand the current state:
- C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\app\layout.tsx (root layout)
- C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\app\page.tsx (homepage)
- C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\app\work\page.tsx (work index)
- C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\app\work\[slug]\page.tsx (project detail)
- C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\app\about\page.tsx (about page)
- C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\app\not-found.tsx (404 page)
- C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\app\globals.css (global styles)
- C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\components\Nav.tsx (navigation)
- C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\components\Footer.tsx (footer)
- C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\components\GridCard.tsx (grid cards)
- C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\components\EditorialGrid.tsx (grid system)
- C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\components\IntroAnimation.tsx (intro)
- C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\lib\projects.ts (project data)
- C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\lib\types.ts (types)
- C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\lib\images.ts (image utilities)
- C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\app\robots.ts (robots)
- C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\app\sitemap.ts (sitemap)
- C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\next.config.ts (next config)
- C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\package.json (dependencies)

After reading all files, produce a comprehensive audit covering:

1. **Accessibility gaps** - Missing ARIA attributes, keyboard navigation issues, focus management, screen reader concerns, color contrast
2. **Performance concerns** - Bundle size, unnecessary client components, image optimization gaps, third-party script loading
3. **SEO gaps** - Missing canonical URLs, structured data improvements, meta tag completeness
4. **UX/UI issues** - Dead ends, missing loading states, error boundaries, responsive edge cases
5. **Security** - CSP headers, external link security, XSS vectors
6. **Code quality** - Unused exports/imports, type safety gaps, consistency issues
7. **Missing features for a portfolio site** - What would a hiring manager or potential client expect?
8. **Mobile experience** - Touch targets, viewport issues, gesture support

For each finding, rate severity (Critical / Important / Nice-to-have) and provide a specific recommendation. Do NOT suggest changes — just audit and report findings.

This is a research task — do not write any code.

content.text:
I now have a comprehensive view of the entire codebase. Here is the full audit.

---

# Comprehensive Audit: jaimeibrahim.com

## 1. Accessibility Gaps

### A1. Skip-to-content link is visually hidden but not keyboard-accessible on focus
**Severity: Critical**
The skip link in `C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\app\layout.tsx` (lines 88-100) uses `position: absolute; left: -9999px` to hide it. This technique does not bring the link on-screen when focused via keyboard. A proper skip link should become visible when `:focus-visible` is applied, so keyboard users can actually see and use it.

### A2. The intro animation overlay blocks screen readers during playback
**Severity: Important**
`C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\components\IntroAnimation.tsx` (line 75) correctly sets `aria-hidden="true"`, but during the 3.1 seconds it is displayed, the main content behind it is not visually accessible and is not hidden from assistive tech. Screen readers could attempt to read the main content while the overlay blocks it visually. There is no `inert` attribute on the `<main>` element during intro playback.

### A3. Mobile hamburger menu lacks `aria-expanded` attribute
**Severity: Important**
In `C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\components\Nav.tsx` (line 81-84), the mobile menu button has `aria-label="Toggle menu"` but is missing `aria-expanded={mobileOpen}`. Screen reader users cannot determine whether the menu is open or closed.

### A4. Mobile dropdown does not trap focus
**Severity: Important**
When the mobile dropdown menu opens (Nav.tsx line 106), keyboard focus is not trapped within it. A user tabbing through will navigate to content behind the overlay. The dropdown also does not close on `Escape` key press.

### A5. Color contrast of `--muted-light` (#999999) against `--bg` (#EEEEEC)
**Severity: Critical**
The contrast ratio of #999999 on #EEEEEC is approximately 2.8:1, which fails WCAG AA for normal text (requires 4.5:1). This color is used extensively: nav links (Nav.module.css line 40), footer info bar (Footer.module.css line 49), back-to-work links, metadata labels, and utility text. A large portion of the site's text fails minimum contrast requirements.

### A6. `--muted` (#767676) on `--bg` (#EEEEEC) is borderline
**Severity: Important**
The contrast ratio of #767676 on #EEEEEC is approximately 4.5:1, just barely passing WCAG AA for normal text at the sizes used (13-15px). This color is used for project descriptions, bio text, client names, and section labels. At 13px, this becomes questionable.

### A7. Grid cards lack meaningful accessible descriptions
**Severity: Important**
In `C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\components\GridCard.tsx`, the entire card is a `<Link>`, but the accessible name derives only from the child text content. When `showText` is `false`, the only accessible name comes from the image alt text. Cards without text blocks have no indication they are navigable project links beyond the image alt.

### A8. Category filter buttons have no `aria-pressed` or `role` context
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
In `C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\components\CategoryFilter.tsx`, the filter buttons do not communicate their selected state to assistive tech. Adding `aria-pressed={active === cat}` would help.

### A9. External links do not indicate they open in a new tab
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
LinkedIn links in the Nav and Footer use `target="_blank"` but provide no visual or accessible indicator (e.g., screen reader text like "opens in new tab") that the user is leaving the site.

### A10. The `<iframe>` for Vimeo embeds has no fallback content
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
In `C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\app\work\[slug]\page.tsx` (lines 106-114), the iframe has a `title` attribute (good) but no fallback content for browsers or assistive tech that cannot render iframes.

---

## 2. Performance Concerns

### P1. Work page (`/work`) is entirely a client component
**Severity: Important**
`C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\app\work\page.tsx` is marked `"use client"` because of the `useState` for the category filter. This means the entire page including the editorial grid, all project data, and all grid cards ship as client-side JavaScript. The project data (12 projects with longDesc, all grid row configurations) is bundled into client JS instead of being server-rendered. Consider lifting the filter state into a client wrapper component while keeping the grid rendering on the server.

### P2. Large image manifest bundled into client JavaScript
**Severity: Important**
`C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\lib\image-manifest.ts` contains paths for ~100+ images. Since it is imported by `images.ts` which is imported by `GridCard.tsx` (a client component), this entire manifest is shipped to the browser. For a growing portfolio, this will only get larger.

### P3. Weather API fetch on every footer mount
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
`C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\components\Footer.tsx` (line 20) fetches weather data from Open-Meteo on every page navigation since the Footer is a client component that remounts. There is no caching layer. While `requestIdleCallback` defers it well, this is still a new network request per navigation.

### P4. No `loading.tsx` suspense boundaries
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
The app has no `loading.tsx` files in any route segment. While the site is statically generated and loads are fast, adding suspense boundaries would improve perceived performance during client-side navigation, especially for the image-heavy project detail pages.

### P5. No explicit `priority` on above-the-fold grid images
**Severity: Important**
In `C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\components\GridCard.tsx`, no images receive `priority={true}`. The hero card (Battle Bank) on the homepage is the LCP candidate but does not get priority loading. Only the project detail page hero image has `priority`.

### P6. Scroll event listeners without throttling
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
Both `ScrollProgress.tsx` and the scroll detection in `Nav.tsx` attach raw scroll listeners. While they use `{ passive: true }`, they fire on every scroll frame. `ScrollProgress` directly mutates DOM style in the handler which is efficient, but Nav's handler triggers `setState` on every scroll event that crosses the 20px threshold (both directions), causing re-renders.

### P7. Framer Motion is listed as a stack decision but not used
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
The CLAUDE.md mentions Framer Motion 11, but it does not appear in `package.json` dependencies. The site uses CSS transitions and IntersectionObserver instead, which is actually better for performance. This is a documentation inconsistency, not a code issue.

---

## 3. SEO Gaps

### S1. Thoughts pages do not exist
**Severity: Important**
The sitemap in `C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\app\sitemap.ts` does not include `/thoughts` or any `/thoughts/[slug]` URLs. More critically, the thoughts route files do not exist at all (the glob returned no files under `src/app/thoughts/`). The nav previously included "Thoughts" in the CLAUDE.md spec, but it has been removed from `Nav.tsx`. However, the `THOUGHTS` array still exists in `C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\lib\projects.ts` (lines 145-150), and the `Thought` type exists in `types.ts`. This is dead code.

### S2. Sitemap `lastModified` is always `new Date()`
**Severity: Important**
In `C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\app\sitemap.ts` (lines 8-10, 14), every URL uses `new Date()` for `lastModified`, meaning every crawl sees "modified today." This undermines the purpose of `lastModified` and could reduce crawl efficiency. Static dates tied to actual content changes would be more useful to search engines.

### S3. No canonical URL on project detail pages
**Severity: Important**
`C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\app\work\[slug]\page.tsx` `generateMetadata` (lines 24-35) does not set a canonical URL or explicit `metadataBase`-relative URL. While Next.js resolves this from the root `metadataBase`, an explicit `alternates: { canonical: ... }` would be more robust, especially for preventing duplicate content issues from trailing slashes or query parameters.

### S4. No structured data for individual projects
**Severity: Important**
The root layout has a `Person` schema.org entry, which is good. But individual project pages (`/work/[slug]`) have no structured data. Adding `CreativeWork` or `VisualArtwork` schema would help portfolio content appear in rich results.

### S5. Missing `og:type` on project detail pages
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
The `generateMetadata` in project detail pages only sets `openGraph.images`. It does not set `og:type` (which defaults to `website` from the parent, but `article` would be more appropriate for case studies).

### S6. No `hreflang` or alternate language signals
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
The site serves English content only and has `lang="en"`. This is fine, but given Bloomberg and GLG are global brands, having explicit `hreflang="en"` in the head would be marginally beneficial.

### S7. OG image for project pages points to raw JPG, not a generated OG image
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
Project OG images (line 32 of `[slug]/page.tsx`) are raw hero JPGs at variable dimensions. OG images should ideally be 1200x630 with text overlay for consistent social media presentation. The root layout references `/opengraph-image` which likely uses Next.js's OG image generation, but individual project pages bypass this.

---

## 4. UX/UI Issues

### U1. Thoughts section is referenced but does not exist
**Severity: Critical**
The `THOUGHTS` data exists, the `Thought` type exists, but there are no page files for `/thoughts` or `/thoughts/[slug]`. If someone navigates to `/thoughts`, they will hit the 404 page. The CLAUDE.md still describes these pages in the "Page Structures" section. Either the pages need to be built or the dead references need to be removed.

### U2. 404 page says "Back to Work" but links to `/`
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
In `C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\app\not-found.tsx` (line 21), the link text says "Back to Work" but the `href` is `/` (homepage). If the user was trying to reach a project, they would expect to land on `/work`, not the homepage.

### U3. No error boundary
**Severity: Important**
There is no `error.tsx` in any route segment. If a runtime error occurs (e.g., image manifest is corrupted, API call fails), the user sees a generic Next.js error page instead of a branded fallback.

### U4. Category filter state is lost on navigation
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
The work page filter uses `useState("All")`. If a user filters to "Identity", clicks a project, then hits the back button, the filter resets to "All". Consider using URL search params (`?category=Identity`) so the filter state persists in browser history.

### U5. Nameplate click forces full page reload
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
In `C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\components\Nav.tsx` (lines 51-63), clicking the nameplate calls `window.location.href = "/"` to replay the intro animation, bypassing Next.js client-side navigation. This means a full page load every time. This is intentional for the intro replay, but it degrades the SPA-like experience. Users who have already seen the intro might prefer a fast navigation home.

### U6. No "back to top" button
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
Project detail pages with many images (e.g., glg-brand with 26 detail images) can be extremely long. The CLAUDE.md mentions a `BackToTop.tsx` component in the architecture, but it does not exist in the codebase.

### U7. Prev/Next navigation at bottom of project pages shows empty `<div>` as placeholder
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
In `C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\app\work\[slug]\page.tsx` (lines 142, 148), when there is no previous or next project, an empty `<div />` is rendered. This is functional but creates an uneven flex layout. Consider hiding the entire navigation row if it is the first or last project, or showing a "Back to all work" fallback.

### U8. The CLAUDE.md spec lists categories that don't match the code
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
The CLAUDE.md lists categories: Identity, Brand Design, Systems, Event Design, Motion, Case Study, Fractional CD, Cutting Room Floor. The actual `Category` type in `C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\lib\types.ts` only has: "Identity", "Design", "Motion". Several projects like "year-ahead" use "Design" instead of "Event Design". This is a documentation drift, not a bug.

---

## 5. Security

### SEC1. No Content Security Policy headers
**Severity: Important**
There is no CSP defined in `next.config.ts` or via middleware headers. The site embeds Vimeo iframes, Google Analytics scripts, and Open-Meteo API calls. Without a CSP, the site is vulnerable to XSS injection via any compromised third-party script. At minimum, a report-only CSP would help monitor violations.

### SEC2. `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` for JSON-LD
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
In `C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\app\layout.tsx` (line 69), `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` is used for the JSON-LD script. The content is a static object so this is safe, but it is worth noting. Next.js 15 supports the `<script type="application/ld+json">` pattern natively in metadata exports, which would be cleaner.

### SEC3. Google Analytics ID exposed via client-side environment variable
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
`C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\components\Analytics.tsx` reads `NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_ID`. This is the expected pattern and not a security risk (GA IDs are public by nature), but it is worth confirming no other `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` variables leak sensitive data.

### SEC4. External links properly use `rel="noopener noreferrer"`
**Severity: N/A (Good)**
All external links in Nav.tsx and Footer.tsx correctly include `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. No issues here.

### SEC5. Vimeo iframe `allow` attribute is broad
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
The iframe in `[slug]/page.tsx` (line 109) allows `autoplay; fullscreen; picture-in-picture`. Consider restricting the `allow` attribute to only what Vimeo needs and adding a `sandbox` attribute for additional isolation.

---

## 6. Code Quality

### CQ1. `THOUGHTS` data and `Thought` type are dead code
**Severity: Important**
`C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\lib\projects.ts` exports `THOUGHTS` (lines 145-150) and `C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\lib\types.ts` exports the `Thought` interface (lines 40-45). No pages consume this data. These are unused exports.

### CQ2. Extensive use of inline styles instead of CSS Modules
**Severity: Important**
While the CLAUDE.md specifies CSS Modules as the styling approach, many pages use inline styles heavily:
- `C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\app\page.tsx` -- almost entirely inline styles
- `C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\app\about\page.tsx` -- almost entirely inline styles
- `C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\app\work\[slug]\page.tsx` -- almost entirely inline styles
- `C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\app\not-found.tsx` -- entirely inline styles

This creates maintenance burden, prevents pseudo-class/pseudo-element usage, and makes responsive overrides difficult. The component files (GridCard, Nav, Footer, EditorialGrid) correctly use CSS Modules, but the page files do not.

### CQ3. Type mismatch: CLAUDE.md Category type vs actual
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
The `Category` type in `types.ts` is `"Identity" | "Design" | "Motion"`. The CLAUDE.md specifies a much broader set. Projects that were originally "Event Design" or "Brand Design" have been collapsed into "Design". This is fine architecturally but the CLAUDE.md is stale.

### CQ4. `detailCount` function in images.ts is exported but never imported
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
`C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\lib\images.ts` exports `detailCount` (line 13). A project-wide search would confirm whether this is used anywhere. Based on the files read, it does not appear in any consumer.

### CQ5. EditorialGrid uses `ri` (row index) as React key
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
In `C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\components\EditorialGrid.tsx` (line 69), the key for grid rows is `ri` (the array index). When filtering changes the array, React may incorrectly reuse DOM nodes. Using a stable key derived from the row's slug composition would be safer.

### CQ6. `isActive` in Nav treats homepage as part of "Work"
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
`C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\components\Nav.tsx` (line 35): `if (href === "/work") return pathname === "/" || pathname.startsWith("/work")`. This means the "Work" nav link appears active when the user is on the homepage. This may be intentional (the homepage shows featured work), but it could confuse users who expect nav state to match the current URL.

---

## 7. Missing Features for a Portfolio Site

### F1. No contact form or direct email link on the homepage
**Severity: Important**
The homepage has no call-to-action for hiring inquiries. The footer CTA says "Let's Work Together" but links to `/about`. The About page has a mailto link, but it is buried in the bio metadata. A hiring manager landing on the homepage has to navigate two pages to find contact info.

### F2. No resume/CV download
**Severity: Important**
For a "Fractional Creative Director" seeking engagements, there is no downloadable PDF resume or CV. Hiring managers and procurement teams often need a PDF to circulate internally.

### F3. No project filtering by year
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
Projects span 2021-2024 but year is not surfaced as a filterable dimension. The year data exists on every project but is not displayed in the grid cards or filter bar.

### F4. No search functionality
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
With 12 projects, search is not critical, but as the portfolio grows, having a quick-filter or search on the work page would help.

### F5. No testimonials or social proof
**Severity: Important**
The About page lists client names but includes no testimonials, LinkedIn recommendations, or quantitative outcomes. Social proof is one of the strongest conversion signals for potential clients.

### F6. No process or methodology page
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
The About page describes what Jaime does but not how. A brief process section (discovery, strategy, design, delivery) would help potential clients understand the engagement model.

### F7. No analytics or engagement tracking beyond GA
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
Vercel Analytics and Speed Insights are integrated (good), but there is no event tracking for meaningful portfolio interactions: which projects are viewed most, how far users scroll on case studies, whether they click the LinkedIn CTA.

### F8. Year is not displayed on grid cards or project detail metadata
**Severity: Nice-to-have**
The `year` field exists on every project object but is not rendered anywhere in the UI. This is useful context for potential clients evaluating recency of work.

---

## 8. Mobile Experience

### M1. Nav breakpoint at 480px is too narrow
**Severity: Important**
The mobile menu in `C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\components\Nav.module.css` (line 147) triggers at `max-width: 480px`. Many modern phones have viewports of 390-428px in portrait, but tablets at 768px still show the desktop three-column nav. Between 481px and 768px, the nav may be cramped with the nameplate and links competing for space, especially since the nav links are 18px/600 weight with letter-spacing.

### M2. Grid card heights are fixed pixel values on mobile
**Severity: Important**
